data.title: Trusted advice, built to last.
data.intro: Northbridge is an independent advisory firm. We help organizations and communities make the decisions that shape them for years, and we stay close until those decisions have taken hold.

children.text: We started Northbridge because we kept seeing the same pattern: good organizations, facing important choices, receiving long reports from people who would not be around to see what happened next.
We work differently. A small team of senior advisers works alongside your people, keeps the analysis proportionate to the decision, and stays involved while the change is made.
Who we work with

Our clients include public bodies, universities, housing and community organizations, and private companies whose work affects the places around them. What they share is a decision that matters and a wish to get it right.
How we are organized

We have four practices: strategic advisory, people and organization, places and infrastructure, and governance and risk. Most engagements draw on more than one of them, so you get one team rather than a set of separate opinions.
Good advice is measured by what is still working five years later.
We are employee-owned and take no commission from suppliers, contractors or software vendors. Our only interest is the quality of your decision.

data.title: How we work
data.intro: Every engagement follows the same simple rhythm, shaped to your situation and your timetable.

children.text: 1. A first conversation
We listen to what you are facing and what a good outcome would look like. There is no charge and no obligation.
2. A short proposal
We describe the questions we would answer, the people involved, the timetable and a fixed fee. You can change the scope before anything starts.
3. Working alongside you
We work in short cycles with your team, sharing findings as we go rather than saving them for a final report.
4. Handover and follow-up
We leave you with clear decisions, owners and the tools to carry on. We check in three and six months later at no extra cost.

data.title: Privacy notice
data.intro: How we handle the information you share with us.

children.text: This website does not use analytics, advertising trackers or cookies of its own.

When you use the contact form, your message is prepared in your own email app and only reaches us if you send that email. We use what you send only to reply to you and to prepare any proposal you ask for.
We keep enquiry emails for up to two years unless we start working together, in which case they become part of the engagement record. You can ask us to delete them at any time.
To ask about your information, write to the enquiries address shown on the contact page.

data.title: Strategic Advisory
data.summary: Clear choices about where to focus, what to stop and how to know it is working.
data.intro: We help boards and leadership teams agree a direction they can explain in a few sentences and act on the following Monday.
data.outcomes:
A shared, honest view of where you stand today
A small number of priorities with owners and dates
A plan your board, staff and partners can test and support
Early measures that show whether the plan is working

children.text: Most organizations do not lack ideas. They lack a shared picture of where they stand and the confidence to say no to good options so they can say yes to the right ones.
What we do

We start by listening to your leadership, your staff and, where it helps, the people you serve. We bring the evidence together into a handful of strategic questions and work through them with you in focused sessions.
Strategy reviews and refreshes
Scenario planning for uncertain markets or funding
Option appraisal for major investments
Board strategy days and facilitated decisions
What changes
You leave with a short strategy, a clear set of priorities and a rhythm for reviewing them, written in your words rather than ours.

data.title: People & Organization
data.summary: Structures, roles and leadership habits that help good people do their best work.
data.intro: We help you design an organization around the work that matters, and bring your people with you through the change.
data.outcomes:
An organization design that follows your strategy
Clear roles, responsibilities and decision rights
A change plan your managers can lead themselves
Leadership development tied to real work

children.text: Reorganizations often redraw boxes without changing how work actually gets done. We start from the work: who decides, who does, and where things get stuck.
What we do
Organization design and operating models
Leadership team development and coaching
Culture and engagement reviews
Change planning and communication
How we work
We involve the people affected early, test designs against real scenarios before anything is announced, and help your managers explain the change in their own words.

data.title: Places & Infrastructure
data.summary: Independent advice on buildings, estates and public spaces that need to serve for decades.
data.intro: We help owners, public bodies and communities decide what to build, refurbish or let go, and how to involve the people who will use it.
data.outcomes:
A clear brief grounded in how spaces will really be used
Options compared on cost, carbon, risk and benefit
Community and stakeholder engagement that informs the plan
A business case ready for funders and approvals

children.text: Buildings and public spaces outlast the plans that created them. Getting the brief right at the start matters more than any later design detail.
What we do
Estate strategies and space reviews
Project briefs and option appraisal
Business cases for capital investment
Community and stakeholder engagement
Independent by design
We do not design or build, and we take no fees from contractors. That lets us give owners and communities a straight view of the choices in front of them.

data.title: Governance & Risk
data.summary: Boards and committees that see the right things in time to act on them.
data.intro: We help boards, trustees and leadership teams strengthen how decisions are made, recorded and followed through.
data.outcomes:
A board and committee structure that fits your size
Risk reporting that highlights what needs a decision
Shorter, clearer papers and better meetings
A practical improvement plan with owners

children.text: Good governance is not more paperwork. It is the right people seeing the right information early enough to act.
What we do
Board effectiveness reviews
Risk frameworks and reporting
Committee terms of reference and delegations
Support for new chairs and trustees
What changes
Meetings get shorter and more decisive, papers become easier to read, and risks are discussed while there is still time to do something about them.

data.title: Planning places people will use for decades
data.excerpt: Buildings outlast the plans that created them. A good brief starts with how a place will really be used in twenty years, not how it looks on opening day.

children.text: Most capital projects are judged on opening day. The people who live and work with them judge them for decades afterwards.
That gap explains many of the problems we are asked to help with: spaces that are hard to adapt, expensive to run or quietly avoided by the people they were built for.
Start with use, not form
Before any drawings, we ask clients to describe a typical week in the building ten years from now. Who arrives first? What happens at lunchtime? What changes in the evening?
Which activities must happen here, and which could happen anywhere?
What will be different in ten years, and what will stay the same?
Who will look after the place, and with what budget?
The cheapest change to a building is the one made in the brief.
Bring the users in early
Engagement works best when there is still something to change. A short series of workshops before the brief is fixed costs little and prevents expensive redesign later.

data.title: Five questions to ask before you reorganize
data.excerpt: A new structure will not fix a decision-making problem. These five questions help leadership teams see what a reorganization can and cannot do.

children.text: Reorganizations are often the first answer to a performance problem and rarely the right one on their own.
The five questions
What decision is not being made today, and who should make it?
Where does work wait, and why?
Which roles overlap, and which gaps does nobody own?
What will managers do differently on the first Monday?
How will we know, in three months, that it is working?
If the answers point to unclear decisions rather than the wrong structure, start there. It is quicker, cheaper and kinder to the people involved.

data.title: Board papers that are easier to decide on
data.excerpt: Long papers rarely lead to better decisions. A simple structure helps boards focus on the choice in front of them.

children.text: Board members often receive hundreds of pages before a meeting. The important decision can be buried on page forty.
A one-page front sheet
We help boards adopt a single front sheet for every paper: the decision needed, the options considered, the recommendation, and the main risks.
What are we being asked to decide?
What happens if we do nothing?
What would change our recommendation?
Supporting detail still matters, but it belongs in appendices. Meetings become shorter, and discussion moves to the questions that need judgement.

data.title: Community engagement that changes the plan
data.excerpt: Consultation that happens after decisions are made builds frustration. Engagement that happens early builds better plans.

children.text: People can tell the difference between being asked and being told. Engagement only builds trust when it can still change something.
Three habits that help
Share options, not a finished answer.
Explain what you heard and what you changed as a result.
Come back when decisions are made, not only when you need support.
If nothing could change, it is a briefing, not a consultation.
Early engagement takes a few extra weeks. It usually saves months later, when objections would otherwise surface at the approval stage.
